A: ["Peremptory norm", "Peremptory norm", "Peremptory norm", "Customary international law", "Peremptory norm", "Peremptory norm", "Customary international law", "Peremptory norm"]
Q: What distinguishes peremptory norms from other principles of customary law?
A: "Peremptory norms, also known as jus cogens, are distinguished from other principles of customary law by their fundamental nature and the fact that they cannot be violated or derogated from by any state through international treaties or local customs. While customary international law can be altered or overridden by treaties, peremptory norms are universally accepted principles that hold a higher status and are considered non-derogable. Examples of peremptory norms include the prohibition of genocide, torture, and slavery, which are recognized by the international community as essential to maintaining fundamental human rights and dignity."
A: Peremptory norms, also known as jus cogens, are distinguished from other principles of customary law by their fundamental nature and the fact that they cannot be violated or derogated from by any state through international treaties or local customs. While customary international law can be altered or overridden by treaties, peremptory norms are universally accepted principles that hold a higher status and are considered non-derogable.
